clue.text: Doctor left a grand for such accommodation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bribed a medic with a thousand pounds in return for lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is a verb here, the anagram signal for LEFT A GRAND. A grand is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground-floor apartment opening onto a garden is one kind of residential accommodation.

clue.text: Tail up crossing line for a medal?

indicators.note: the reversed word straddles the single letter, holding it inside
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them, to dog them

explanation.surface: A question about whether a raised tail earns a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is the top award at the Olympics, an example of a medal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Take to task, looking embarrassed about prudish article

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the inner pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: someone embarrassed looks red in the face
prim means prudish, easily shocked
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A blushing person scolds about a straitlaced newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to task is to scold or rebuke them formally, a synonym.

clue.text: Improve workers in education

indicators.note: the workers are placed inside the abbreviation for education

parts.note: men can mean workers, as in a firm's staff

explanation.surface: A call to raise standards by putting staff into schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and so better it, a synonym of improve.

clue.text: Overweight animals — some getting too much bread?

definitions.meaning: bread is slang for money; wealthy people paid excessively are called this

explanation.surface: Plump pets that are being given too much to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means chubby moggies; idiomatically it means overpaid rich people, bread being money.

clue.text: Helped a cook set up to include five

indicators.note: the earlier pieces take in the Roman numeral, holding it inside
in a down clue, set up means the name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British television cookery writer
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone assisted a chef in arranging things for five people.
explanation.walkthrough: The cook is Delia Smith, Britain's best-known TV cookery writer; 'set up' reads her name upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Availed is an old-fashioned word for helped or was of use to, a synonym.

clue.text: Small fortune offering vacancy

parts.note: lot means fate or fortune, one's lot in life

explanation.surface: A modest sum of money offered with a job opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is an opening or position available to be filled, a synonym of vacancy.

clue.text: Forbidden city Liverpool has always embraced

indicators.note: the letters sit held within the phrase Liverpool has always

explanation.surface: A claim that a northern English football city has long loved some exotic place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan capital was long closed to foreigners and known as the Forbidden City.

clue.text: Regulator needing drink container and pastry right away

parts.note: a Thermos is a vacuum flask for drinks

indicators.note: right is sent away, removed from the pastry word

parts.note: a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: A supervisor who needs a flask and a pie straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately', but it is R removed from TART, giving TAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat controls temperature automatically, so it is a regulating device.

clue.text: Animal quietly lying in ground

indicators.note: the musical letter lies inside the word for ground

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A creature keeping still in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a freshwater turtle, an example of an animal.

clue.text: A note in case of late error

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the outer letters of late
the case of a word is its outer letters, here first and last

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: An added memo in a tardy situation was a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor mistake, a synonym of error.

clue.text: Brand new teen drama

indicators.note: these letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A television label introduces a fresh show about adolescents.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the name under which a product is sold, a synonym of brand.

clue.text: Bonus of seeing Germany collapse after victory?

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the word for victory

parts.note: a win is a victory
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
to fall is to collapse

explanation.surface: A sporting reward from watching the Germans fold after a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is an unexpected gain or piece of good fortune, a synonym of bonus.

clue.text: Paper encompassing Liberal's field of study

indicators.note: the paper word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, the political party

explanation.surface: A newspaper covering a political party's area of research.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or sphere, such as a field of study or knowledge.

clue.text: Setter upset about communist having such acceptability?

indicators.note: the word setter is knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is annoyed about a leftist being so respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is standing or credibility among fashionable young people, a kind of acceptability.

clue.text: Drink container mostly for trains

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a chest is a container

explanation.surface: A box for tea that is mainly used for railway carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like railway stock but is a verb, to coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to train or instruct, so teaches matches trains as verbs.

clue.text: Energy taken from fever rampant in blessed insect

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for blessed

parts.note: holy means blessed or sacred

indicators.note: rampant means running wild, so the letters are rearranged
energy is removed from the word fever

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Losing vigour from a raging illness inside a sacred bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes E from FEVER, leaving FVER; 'rampant' makes it VERF, which goes into HO-LY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoverfly is a small fly that hovers, an example of an insect.

clue.text: Papers on low exam grades cause unhappiness

indicators.note: the papers come on, after, the grades

parts.note: D and E are low exam grades
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: Newspaper reports about poor results make people miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress someone is to make them gloomy or dejected, causing unhappiness.

clue.text: Simple professor's comfortable spot?

parts.note: easy means simple
a chair is a professor's post at a university

explanation.surface: A straightforward academic's cosy place to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a padded armchair, a comfortable place to sit.

clue.text: I've invested in tips for salad leaves

indicators.note: the contraction is placed inside the word for tips

parts.note: ends are tips, extremities

explanation.surface: Someone has put money into advice for greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Endives are leafy chicory plants whose leaves go in salads.

clue.text: Lawman may be fresh if in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disarray, rearranged

explanation.surface: A law officer could be cheeky if things go badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a law-enforcement officer, especially in the American West.

clue.text: Condition of men struggling in continent

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the continent

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: the letters of men struggle, writhing into a new order

explanation.surface: The situation of men having a hard time somewhere in a large landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia, loss of memory, is a medical condition.

clue.text: Entertainer embraced by sweetheart is tearful

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the phrase sweetheart is tearful

explanation.surface: A performer, cuddled by a loved one, weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Cat and dog ultimately in row

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of dog

explanation.surface: A cat and a dog have a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel (rhyming with cow) but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is the largest of the big cats.

clue.text: Supported conduct in speech

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to guide is to conduct or lead

explanation.surface: Someone backed good behaviour in a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope that steadies a tent or mast, so guyed means held up by such ropes.

clue.text: Admission of charm

definitions.meaning: the act of coming in or right of access
to captivate or delight, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a way in or admittance; as a verb, stressed differently, it means to enchant.

clue.text: Down under a student grant

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word for down sits beneath the other pieces

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a British L-plate
low means down, dispirited

explanation.surface: In Australia, a learner gets financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' looks like Australia, but it splits into LOW placed under A L.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a request is to allow or permit it, a synonym.

clue.text: Understands touring cars must bear east

indicators.note: the cars carry the letter within them

parts.note: GT is gran turismo, a grand touring car; GTS is plural

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a motorcade has to veer eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to understand it, as in 'I get it'.

clue.text: Payments as a result of links to the monarchy

parts.note: royal means of or relating to the monarchy
ties are links or connections

explanation.surface: Money comes in because of connections with the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links to the monarchy' is ROYAL TIES read as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalties are sums paid to authors or patent holders for each sale or use of their work.

clue.text: Renounce time off work

definitions.meaning: to give up or abandon, as when quitting a post
a holiday or period of absence granted by an employer

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to abandon or depart from; as a noun it means permitted absence from a job.

clue.text: Odd about duck being an extinct species

indicators.note: the letters of odd are turned about, rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A strange thing about a waterbird belonging to a vanished type.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricketer's score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless Mauritian bird died out in the 17th century and is the classic example of an extinct species.

clue.text: Pudding must include minor responsibility later

indicators.note: the pudding word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding, the dessert course
a ward is a minor under someone's care

explanation.surface: Dessert has to come with a small duty after the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the dessert course is informally called 'afters'; a ward is a child in a guardian's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards means at a later time, so it substitutes for later as an adverb.
